title: Check frontend circular import count with yarn lint:circular
answers: How do I check if a change introduces a circular dependency?
How many circular import paths does the frontend have?
body: Run `yarn lint:circular` to get the total count of circular import paths across the frontend bundle graph. A focused scan rooted at public/app/app.ts narrows this to paths reachable at app startup (eager cycles), which matter more for bundle/startup cost than deep lazy cycles. Use before/after counts to confirm a dependency-cycle fix actually reduced paths rather than just relocating the cycle. Baseline observed in this PR: 326 total paths / 231 from the app.ts scan after the fix (down from 233; total down from 326 to 324).
applies: Any frontend PR touching module import graphs in public/app/**
says: How do I check if my code change introduced a circular dependency?
What is the total number of circular import paths in the frontend?
How can I verify that a circular import fix actually worked?
Does my change increase the number of circular dependencies in the bundle?
What happens if I run the circular import checker before and after?
search: Run `yarn lint:circular` (defined in package.json) to count circular import paths in the frontend bundle; narrow focus to public/app/app.ts to detect only eager cycles at startup, which impact bundle and startup cost more than deep lazy cycles. Compare before/after counts to confirm a dependency-cycle fix reduced paths rather than relocating the issue. Apply when frontend PRs modify module imports in public/app/** to verify the change actually breaks circular paths.
